title: Een koffie, graag
subtitle: Ordering in a café
intro: After this lesson you can order a drink politely at a Dutch café and ask for the bill. You will also learn the articles een, de and het, and when to use alstublieft or alsjeblieft.

words.note: A mass noun: 'een koffie' means one cup of coffee.

example.nl: Mag ik een glas water, alstublieft?
example.en: May I have a glass of water, please?

example.nl: Zij wil graag een glas wijn.
example.en: She would like a glass of wine.

words.note: A diminutive of kop, so it takes het.

example.en: May I have the bill, please?

words.note: Formal: to a waiter, a stranger, or more than one person.
Informal: to friends, family and children.
Use u with the waiter or people you do not know.
Graag makes a request polite; it does not mean 'like' here.

grammar.title: een, de and het
grammar.explanation: Dutch has one word for 'a/an': **een**. For 'the' there are two words: **de** and **het**. Most nouns take **de**; a smaller group takes **het**, so learn the article with every new noun.
grammar.tip: Always learn a noun with its article: not koffie, but de koffie.

grammar.title: Polite ordering: Ik wil graag..., Mag ik...?, ... graag
grammar.explanation: To order politely, use **Ik wil graag** + the thing: **Ik wil graag een koffie**. You can also ask **Mag ik** + the thing: **Mag ik een glas water?** A short, very common order is the thing + **graag**: **Een koffie, graag.**

rows: May I have a glass of water?

examples.en: May I have a glass of water?

grammar.tip: Put graag after the thing you want: Een koffie, graag.

grammar.title: Formal and informal: alstublieft / alsjeblieft
grammar.explanation: Use **u** forms with a waiter, a stranger, or a group you address formally: **alstublieft**, **dank u wel**, **Wilt u...?**. Use **je/jij** forms with friends, family and children: **alsjeblieft**, **dank je wel**, **Wil je...?**.
grammar.tip: When in doubt with an adult you do not know, use the u form; it is never rude.

exercises.explain: Adding graag makes the order sound polite and friendly.

exercises.explain: The thing + alstublieft is a polite request.

exercises.prompt: In 'Ik wil graag een kopje thee', what does graag do?
exercises.explain: Graag softens a request and makes it polite.
Use 'Ik wil graag' + thing for a polite order; graag can also go at the end.

mistakes.pattern: Puts graag before wil in a statement: 'Ik graag wil een koffie'.
mistakes.explain: Put graag after wil or after the noun: 'Ik wil graag een koffie' / 'Een koffie, graag'.

culture.title: Paying and tipping
culture.text: In the Netherlands you usually pay by card; in shops and cafés you will hear the verb pinnen (to pay by debit card). Cash is accepted in most places, but some cafés are card-only. Tipping is not compulsory: rounding up the bill or leaving about 5-10% in a restaurant is normal for good service, and in a café it is often just a rounding-up or nothing.

summary: Use een for 'a/an' and de or het for 'the'; learn each noun with its article.
Order politely with Ik wil graag..., Mag ik...? or just the thing + graag.
Use alstublieft and dank u wel with u (formal); alsjeblieft and dank je wel with friends.
Ask for the bill with De rekening, alstublieft.
In the Netherlands, paying by card is called pinnen.
